references.text: The Israelites also complained in the Desert of Sin that they had been brought out of Egypt only to die of hunger, echoing the same theme of grumbling against Moses and God.
The people quarreled with Moses and complained about the lack of water, asking why he had brought them out of Egypt just to let them die of thirst.
The Israelites complained about the food and longed for what they had eaten in Egypt, showing similar dissatisfaction with the manna.
The people grumbled against Moses and Aaron, wishing they had died in Egypt, following the same pattern of complaint and rebellion.
The people quarreled with Moses at Meribah, complaining about the lack of water and food, and regretting that they had left Egypt.
A description of the manna that the house of Israel called 'manna,' the bread from heaven which the people now despised.
The psalm describes how the people spoke against God and asked if He could set a table in the wilderness, poetically recounting their grumbling.
The psalm mentions how the Israelites grumbled in their tents and did not listen to the voice of the Lord.
Paul warns against testing Christ, as some of the Israelites did and were killed by snakes, directly referencing the consequences of this grumbling.
Jesus refers to Moses lifting up the snake in the wilderness, which happened as a result of the people's sin described in this text.
